text:
morgan: Heads-up, repro for a weird AsyncClient + FastAPI lifespan thing in our sampleapp tests.

morgan: Running pytest against the sampleapp (uvicorn in test-mode) sometimes fails with `RuntimeError: no running event loop` coming from httpx when we call `asyncio.create_task` in startup.

sam: can you paste the minimal snippet?

morgan: sure:
```py
# app/main.py (startup)
from fastapi import FastAPI
import httpx, asyncio

app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup():
    client = httpx.AsyncClient()
    # kicks off background task that uses client extensively
    asyncio.create_task(background_worker(client))

async def background_worker(client):
    await client.get("http://localhost:8000/health")
```

morgan: In tests we use TestClient and run `pytest` (sync) with a fixture that imports the app. Intermittently httpx complains about missing loop from `asyncio.create_task`.

lina: hmm. TestClient spins up its own loop in a thread sometimes. Are you using `anyio` pytest plugin or `pytest-asyncio`?

morgan: pytest-asyncio not used. It's a plain sync test that relies on TestClient. The intermittent nature makes me think of import-time event loop vs thread-local loop mismatch.

sam: two quick suspects: 1) AsyncClient created outside an active loop (but in an async startup it should be fine). 2) `asyncio.create_task` needs a running loop in the current thread — if TestClient runs the app in another thread, create_task may refer to the wrong loop.

lina: try using `asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(...)` inside startup instead of `asyncio.create_task`, that binds to the currently running loop. Or wrap background tasks with `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` if running sync.

morgan: tried `asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task` and it improved stability but still fails in CI sometimes. Repro seems easier when tests import sampleapp before pytest starts event loop fixtures.

sam: could be a lifecycle ordering bug in our sampleapp template. We create an AsyncClient at module import in some helper — that will obviously be out-of-loop. Make sure AsyncClient is created inside startup or lazily when first needed.

morgan: confirmed one helper was creating a global AsyncClient at import for convenience. Moving it into startup/cleanup fixes > 95% repros. But still one flake where TestClient's thread teardown races with our background task shutdown and httpx complains about closed transport.

lina: add a proper shutdown handler that cancels background tasks and awaits client.aclose(). Example:
```py
@app.on_event("shutdown")
async def shutdown():
    for t in BACKGROUND_TASKS:
        t.cancel()
    await client.aclose()
```

morgan: implemented shutdown cleanup in the sampleapp PR and added a small test that uses `with TestClient(app) as tc:` and waits for tasks to finish. CI run now passed 10/10 locally.

qa-bot: quick note: left a failing CI log at https://ci.internal/12345 showing one run with `ConnectionResetError` during shutdown — looks consistent with abrupt thread stop.

sam: for SDK guidance, maybe we should add a short note in our devex docs explaining common FastAPI/TestClient pitfalls with AsyncClient and background tasks and recommend the pattern: create client in startup, create tasks with `get_running_loop().create_task`, and gracefully shutdown.

morgan: agreed. I'll open a small doc PR under devex/samples and update the sampleapp template. Also adding a unit test that runs the app in-process to catch this in CI.

devex-bot: action created: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/pulls/428 — updates sampleapp startup/shutdown patterns + docs.

lina: one more thought — could we add a convenience helper in the Python SDK that provides a lifecycle-aware AsyncClient factory for frameworks (FastAPI/Starlette) to reduce user mistakes? e.g., `provide_async_client(app, *, base_url=None)` that wires startup/shutdown and stores client on app.state.

sam: yes please. File an issue in the SDK repo and tag it `good-first-pr` for platform engineers.

morgan: filed: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/issues/310 — description + repro snippet + proposed helper API.

morgan: thanks all, closing the loop here. :tada:
